title: Power Bulk 5
author: Kevin M.
desc:
Power Bulk 5 was designed as an Upper/Lower split with higher concentration on Chest and Lats fast growth!  The 3 Upper days all start with a chest press and end with conventional pull-ups.  This gives me more reps to get better with pullups throughout the week! 

In order to not have 20 exercises a day on Upper days, these are split with a secondary focus.  Ex. Upper A (Chest/Shoulders), Upper B (Chest/Arms), Upper C (Chest/Back).  I prefer the split to be Day 1 Upper A, Day 2 Lower A, Day 3 Rest, Day 4 Upper B, Day 5 Lower B, Day 6 Upper C, Day 7 Rest.   Typically, Mon., Tues, Rest, Thur., Fri., Sat., Rest.

This program also focuses on progressive overloading with adding an extra set on the second week, then adding extra weight for the 3rd and 4th week and a De-Load every 5th week. 

Two Major Compound lifts in this program (Bench Press/Barbell Squat) is non-conventional with Low Reps but High Sets.  Example: instead of 3 sets of 6 to 8 for compound, we'll do 6 sets of 3 reps.  This allows to push heavier weight without getting fatigued as fast.  If need be, by sets 6 or 7 even, drop the weight a little to get the 3 or 4 reps in.  All these short sets should be around RPE 9!    The remaining of the workout program is all more typical 3 sets of 8 to 10 or 10 to 12.  

I originally set it up for 4 months in length.  It's basically 3 months of hard lifting with 3 De-Load Weeks included to help with recovery.  Starting out should take on average 90 to 120 mins as you get use to it, but then it should stay under 90 mins.  Rest times should never be over 2 to 3 mins, even with the Low rep/High set compounds, you only need to rest about 2 mins tops between sets.   Some exercises can easily be put into Supersets to keep things moving as well.
